business.offering: Reusable kitchenware and thoughtful home storage
business.channels: Online shop and two neighborhood stores

question: Explore an explicitly hypothetical trial. Finance should use calculate_javascript with units 120, price 25, and unit cost 17, then publish an illustrative bar chart of revenue, total cost and gross profit. Operations should publish a decision flowchart. Skeptic should challenge the assumptions. Chair should publish a self-contained interactive HTML quantity slider showing revenue at the hypothetical price. Each seat should do its own part. Label all outputs illustrative and cite executed results.

artifacts.title: Illustrative hypothetical trial unit economics
assumptions: All stated units sell at the hypothetical price.
Unit cost applies to every sold unit; no other costs, taxes, discounts, returns, or overhead are included.
artifacts.code: (input) => { const revenue = input.units * input.price; const totalCost = input.units * input.unitCost; const grossProfit = revenue - totalCost; return {units: input.units, price: input.price, unitCost: input.unitCost, revenue, totalCost, grossProfit}; }

claims.text: Under the stated assumptions, the derived scenario gives revenue of "3000", total cost of "2040", and gross profit of "960". The calculation assumes all units sell at the hypothetical price and excludes taxes, discounts, returns, overhead, and other costs. [Illustrative chart: R1F2]

uncertainties: The assumed trial volume, price, unit cost, and sell-through are unverified; actual results may differ.
The chart is illustrative and excludes costs beyond the stated unit cost.

turns.summary: I support Finance’s illustrative economics as a conditional scenario, not evidence of expected performance. The decision flowchart recommends validating assumptions, running a bounded trial, and reviewing actual results before considering scale. [R1F1; R1O1]

claims.text: The flowchart is an illustrative decision aid: validate the assumptions, track actual sales and costs in a bounded trial, and consider scaling only after reviewing verified results against decision criteria. [R1O1]

uncertainties: The hypothetical inputs and assumptions have not been independently verified; actual demand, sell-through, and costs remain unknown. [R1F1]

turns.summary: I qualify Operations’ proposed trial-and-review path: it is a cautious decision aid, not evidence that a trial is ready or that the scenario’s inputs are realistic. The assumption-check flowchart makes those validation gates explicit. [R1F1; R1O1; R1S2]

claims.text: The calculation is conditional on all assumed units selling at the hypothetical price and the stated unit cost applying to each sold unit; it excludes taxes, discounts, returns, overhead, and other costs. [R1F1]
The assumption-check flowchart is illustrative: validate inputs before a bounded trial, then review actual results before considering scale. [R1S2]

challenges.text: Operations’ suggestion to run a bounded trial should not be read as evidence that demand, sell-through, unit cost, or omitted costs are known; those assumptions remain unverified. [R1F1; R1O1]

uncertainties: The supplied evidence does not establish whether the hypothetical inputs reflect feasible trial conditions or actual business performance. [R1F1]

turns.summary: I accept Skeptic’s warning: this slider illustrates the hypothetical price assumption, not validated demand or expected performance. [R1F1; R1C1]

claims.text: The self-contained slider displays revenue as quantity changes at a fixed hypothetical price; it is illustrative and does not verify inputs or forecast sales. [R1F1; R1C1]

challenges.text: Skeptic’s challenge is well-founded: the scenario assumes all stated units sell at the hypothetical price and excludes other costs, so neither the calculation nor slider establishes trial readiness. [R1F1]

uncertainties: Actual demand, sell-through, price feasibility, and complete costs are not established. [R1F1]

decision.action: Treat the interactive slider as an illustrative exploration only; do not use it as a forecast or evidence of business performance. [R1F1; R1C1]

rationale.text: The artifact is explicitly illustrative and uses a fixed hypothetical price; its output changes with the selected quantity. [R1F1; R1C1]
Operations’ proposed validate-then-review pathway is a decision aid, not evidence that a trial is ready. [R1O1; R1S2]
